newsitem.title: TURKEY: Islamist protesters clash with police in Turkey.
newsitem.headline: Islamist protesters clash with police in Turkey.

text.p: Police fired water cannon and used batons to break up a crowd of about 2,000 Islamists protesting in Istanbul against a secularist education bill after Friday midday prayers, witnesses said.
Clashes broke out as police blocked the path of protesters trying to march from a mosque in Istanbul's Cagaloglu district to present a statement to a nearby local education directorate.

Police moved in on the demonstrators with armoured cars equipped with water cannon. Some of the protesters attempted to climb onto one of the vehicles but were beaten back by the high-pressure water and the blows of police batons.

Several of the protesters were dragged bleeding away from the scene. State-run Anatolian news agency later said 66 people arrested at the protest. At least one policeman was also injured in the fighting.
Elsewhere in Turkey, 13 people were detained in the western city of Bursa and 10 in southeastern Bingol. Police also dispersed protests in Konya and Sanliurfa, the agency said.

The trouble flared as parliament resumed debate on a draft law to extend compulsory state education to eight years from five. The law would effectively lead to the closure of the first section of religious schools, known as "Imam Hatips".
"Imam Hatips cannot be closed," the protesters chanted as they left the mosque in the historic heart of Istanbul.

The protests have become a weekly event in Istanbul and in towns elsewhere in Turkey, prompting tight security outside mosques for the Friday ceremonies, the most important prayers of the Moslem week.

The education plans were a central element of demands by the secularist military in Febrary aimed at cracking down on an alleged rise in Islamist activism while the Islam-based Welfare Party was in power.

Turkey's first Islamist leader Necmettin Erbakan resigned as prime minister in June under the secularist pressure. His government was replaced by a right-left coalition under Mesut Yilmaz which promised to press through the army's demands.
